City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
June 13, 2017
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 06:01 p.m. , on June 13, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on June 08, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Mayor Buknum
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
Council Member Goodell
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Raths
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Presentation on the Orange County District Attorney's Efforts to Combat Human Exploitation and Trafficking
The presentation was postponed to the meeting of June 27, 2017.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Ronald Eroh and Susmitha Valvekar, M.V.: on behalf of the Cultural Arts Committee, they invited the City Council Members to the 2017 Mission Viejo Photographer's Exhibit reception on July 14, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. at the Mission Viejo Library.
Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: discussed the content of the May 9, 2017, City Council Meeting Minutes.
Judy Fike, M.V.: asked that the City create a Mission Viejo Climate Action Plan.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the Consent Calendar as outlined below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Buknum, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, Council Member Goodell, Council Member Kelley, and Council Member Raths
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approve the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declare that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approve the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of May 23, 2017, as presented or as amended.
3.
Check Register Dated May 12, 2017 in the Amount of $1,125,962.34
Ratify the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register Dated May 19, 2017 in the Amount of $1,513,759.91
Ratify the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register Dated May 26, 2017 in the Amount of $828,592.66
Ratify the accompanying check register.
6.
City Treasurerâ€™s Monthly Report for April 2017
Receive and file.
7.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurerâ€™s Monthly Report for April 2017
Receive and file.
8.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurerâ€™s Monthly Report for April 2017
Receive and file.
9.
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurerâ€™s Monthly Report for April 2017
Receive and file.
10.
Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo â€“ Third Quarter of 2016-17
Receive and file.
11.
Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services
Approve the Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs for State legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed the amount of $120,000 for the period of July 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019.
12.
Annual Facility Janitorial Maintenance Amendment 2017-2019
(1) Approve the Third Amendment to the existing contract (A15-45) with Team One Management for the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $617,080.00 and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order to Team One Management for the period of July 1 2017 to June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $308,450.00.
13.
Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract
(1) Approve County Agreement with the County of Orange for the period July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019 in the amount of $2,054,102.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2018 in an amount not to exceed $1,027,051.00, pending adoption of the 2017-2019 budget by City Council.
14.
Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre – Year 2017 – Phase 1
(1) Adopt Resolution 17-21 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing Protests; (2) instruct the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instruct the City Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 22, 2017.
15.
Alicia Parkway Landscape Slope Renovation - West Coast Arborist, Inc.
(1) Approve Contract Amendment #20 in the amount of $40,000 to West Coast Arborist Inc. for additional trimming and selected removal of trees along Alicia Parkway in the next phase of landscape slope renovations.
16.
Annual City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M2 Eligibility Submittal to the Orange County Transportation Authority
(1) Adopt Resolution 17-22 Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program Beginning with the 2017-2018 Fiscal Year; (2) adopt Resolution 17-23 Concerning the Status and Update of the General Plan Circulation Element and Mitigation Fee Program for the Renewed Measure M (M2) Program; and (3) direct staff to transmit said resolutions to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) by June 30, 2017, to maintain the City?s continued eligibility in receiving Fiscal Year 2017-18 Renewed Measure M (M2) local fair-share revenues and in pursuing competitive grant funding opportunities.
17.
2016 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)-Notice of Completion
(1) Certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
18.
Oso Parkway/Interstate 5 Northbound On-ramp Improvements (CIP 16226)
Authorize staff to issue a purchase order to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $225,000 for final design services related to the widening of the northbound Interstate 5 on-ramp at Oso Parkway.
19.
Request for a one-time exemption to the â€œNo Alcoholic Beverage Consumptionâ€ Regulation at City Facilities for Library program.
Approve the request for a one-time exemption to the ?No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption? Regulation at City facilities.
20.
Second Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and Processing Agreement
(1) Approve the Second Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and Processing Agreement with Baker and Taylor, Inc., for the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2019 in the amount of $400,000; and
(2) Authorize issuance of a purchase order to Baker and Taylor, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $200,000 pending adoption of the 2017-19 budget by the City Council.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS
21.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.
22.
Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
23.
Review of 2017-19 Proposed Budget
City Manager Dennis Wilberg provided a summary of past public meetings on the budget and stated that the budget has been well addressed.
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and outlined the proposed 2017-19 budget.
The Council Members made comments and staff provided answers to budget-related questions.
The City Council received and filed the report.
24.
Council Policy No. 0300-8 - Management and Budget Policies
Dyas presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1) adopt Resolution 17-24 Revising Council Policy No 0300-8 - Management and Budget Policies and Amending the City Council Policy Manual to Include Said Revisions; (2) adopt Resolution 17-25 Establishing the General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for the 2017-19 Budget Cycle.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Buknum, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, Council Member Goodell, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
Council Member Raths
ABSENT:
None
25.
Status Update on Drug Prevention Coalition
Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the report.
Margie Fleitman, Solace Orange County Grief Recovery/Support Group, M.V.: announced that she is one of the co-founders of Solace which provides a weekly support meeting for those who have lost a loved to substance use disorder, or are currently struggle with a loved one's substance use disorder. They also provides community members with overdose recognition and response training and Nnaloxone, a life-saving overdose reversal antidote. She expressed her interest in supporting the City's efforts with a Drug Prevention Coalition.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
26.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Goodell
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley apologized for missing the last Council Meeting and the Memorial Day ceremony. Traveled to Indiana to see her youngest son receive his Masters of Divinity from Southern Baptist _______.
Council Member Raths
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
Mayor Bucknum
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 8:52 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 9:48 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-571-01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN 808-720-12, APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative Services Director Dyas, City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.
CS2.
Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.
CS3.
Conference with Legal Counsel; Initiation of Litigation pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision 54956.9 (1 potential case).
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Curley announced that the City Council considered three Closed Session matters and there was no reportable action.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 27, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.
